subskill: No-solution value places the extreme solutions
prompt:
kx + 93 = 7x + 15k
In the equation above, k is a constant. Ana solves the equation for each integer k from 5 to 19, inclusive, for which it has a solution. What is the difference between the greatest and the least of the solutions she finds?
explanation: Collect the x terms: kx - 7x = 15k - 93, so (k - 7)x = 15k - 93. When k = 7 this reads 0 = 12, so there is no solution and Ana finds nothing for k = 7. For every other k, x = (15k - 93)/(k - 7) = 15 + 12/(k - 7). For k greater than 7 the fraction is positive and largest when k - 7 is smallest, so the greatest solution is at k = 8: x = 27. For k less than 7 the fraction is negative and most negative when 7 - k is smallest, so the least solution is at k = 6: x = 3. The difference is 27 - 3 = 24. Choice 7 comes from assuming the solution changes steadily with k, so the extremes are at the ends of the range: x = 9 at k = 5 and x = 16 at k = 19; but k = 7, where there is no solution, lies inside the range and the solution runs off to large and small values beside it. Choice 13 finds the least solution at k = 6 but still takes the greatest at the end of the range, k = 19. Choice 30 adds the greatest and least solutions instead of subtracting.
solve: const xs = []; for (let k = 5; k <= 19; k++) { if (k === 7) continue; xs.push((15 * k - 93) / (k - 7)); } return String(Math.max(...xs) - Math.min(...xs));

distractor_solve.7: const x = k => (15 * k - 93) / (k - 7); return String(Math.abs(x(19) - x(5)));
distractor_solve.13: const xs = []; for (let k = 5; k <= 19; k++) { if (k === 7) continue; xs.push((15 * k - 93) / (k - 7)); } const x19 = (15 * 19 - 93) / (19 - 7); return String(x19 - Math.min(...xs));
distractor_solve.30: const xs = []; for (let k = 5; k <= 19; k++) { if (k === 7) continue; xs.push((15 * k - 93) / (k - 7)); } return String(Math.max(...xs) + Math.min(...xs));

mechanism: extremes beside the no-solution value, then subtract
quantity_asked: the greatest minus the least of the solutions for the integers k from 5 to 19 that give a solution

setup.i: k is in the x-coefficient on one side and in the constant on the other side of a one-variable equation, so the solution is 15 + 12/(k - 7) and k = 7 gives no solution
setup.ii: over the integers k in a stated range other than 7, the solution is greatest and least at the integers on either side of 7, not at the ends of the range
setup.iii: difference between the greatest and least solutions

plugback.aggregate_over: the solutions for the integers k from 5 to 19 other than 7: the greatest (at k = 8) minus the least (at k = 6)

30.why: Adding instead of subtracting moves the result up or down depending on the sign of the least solution, which the stem does not show.
